newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Gold Fields raises A$48.75 mln.
newsitem.headline: Australian Gold Fields raises A$48.75 mln.

text.p: Gold explorer Australian Gold Fields NL said on Friday it had raised A$48.8 million through a a A$38.8 million placement of 45.6 million new shares and a A$10 million issue of convertible notes.
The funds were raised to fund the acquisition, exploration and development of the Morobe gold project in Papua New Guinea, Australian Gold Fields said.
The 45.6 million share placement was managed by Prudential Bache Securities and sold at 85 cents per share.
Australian Gold Fields said it reserved the right to place up to 53 million shares in total in response to strong investor demand. The issue is subject to shareholder approval.
The convertible note issue is of five million notes at A$2.00 each redeemable on December 31. They can be redeemed at A$2.00 per share during 1998 and attract interest of five percent per year.

"It is a convincing endorsement of our plans in Papua New Guinesa, where we are on track to commission a new gold mine producing at an annual rate of 200,000 ounces by the end of next year and to substantially expand the project in future," Australian Gold Fields Cyril Quek said in a statement.
"We will immediately undertake resource and reserve drilling metallurgical test work and a bankable feasibility study to mine the Morobe gold project," he said.

A independent review of the Morobe project had concluded it had resources in four deposits totalling 70.7 million tonnes at an average grade of 2.3 grams per tonne representing 5.24 million ounces of gold.
"We have been advised the potential exists to substantially increase this resource base by exploring a further 40 gold prospects," Quek said.

Australian Gold Field planned to develop Morobe in two stages, starting with reserve definition drilling and metallurgical test work to establish a reserve of six million to 7.5 million tonnes of near-surface ore at 4.5 grams per tonne.

A US$60-65 million processing plant would be built with a starting capacity of 1.2-1.5 million tonnes and gold recoveries of 90 percent to produce at the rate of 200,000 ounces of gold by the end of the December quarter next year (1998).
The second stage would be to expand the plant to three million tonnes a year.
Australian Gold Fields' shares closed up one cent at A$1.00.
